segments.title: Cold open
sentences: This is a frame from a finished film.
It came from one sentence: you hold the A key, and a voice wakes up.
Between the sentence and the frame sit a script, a voice, a timeline, a renderer, a mix and the gates.
A one-off film is a memory. A series is a system.
segments.notes: Open on a real Wave frame. Pull back to the sentence that produced it. End on the thesis.

segments.title: Three layers
sentences: The machine lives in explainer-kit: render, voice, mix, master and verify.
The brain is a skill: when to run each command, and what to check.
The content lives in the project: script, scenes, captures, music.
Numbers in the kit, procedure in the skill, content in the project.
segments.notes: Three stacked bands with a hard boundary between them. Light each band on its sentence.

segments.title: One command
sentences: A new film starts with one command.
explainer init writes the explainer folder and pins the kit version.
config.json names the few things a project may change.
script.json holds the argument, scenes.js draws it, assets.js names the captures.
segments.notes: Terminal card on the left, file tree on the right. The kit pin is coral.

segments.title: The spine
sentences: The script is the spine.
Ten chapters, one idea each, three to five sentences.
Write for the ear: second person, present tense, short clauses.
Read it aloud with a timer. The target is three fifteen.
segments.notes: Ten chapter blocks. One chapter opens into its sentences. A 3:15 timer arc fills.

segments.title: The clock
sentences: Narration turns sentences into time.
One house voice reads each line, cached by a hash of text and settings.
The kit measures every clip and writes timeline.json.
Run it again, and the same words land at the same times.
segments.notes: Sentence to hash to cached audio to measured blocks to timeline.json. Real Wave times: 43.920 to 47.120.

segments.title: Drawing time
sentences: Scenes are functions, not slides.
Each segment id maps to a function of time and timeline.
The diagram builds as the sentence explains it, then holds.
The kit supplies the frame, type and chrome. The project supplies the argument.
segments.notes: Show the function signature, then the voice frame with a time readout. The diagram is tied to sentence beats.

segments.title: Look first
sentences: A full render takes minutes. A still takes seconds.
The stills command draws one frame per chapter.
You look at all ten before the encode.
serve opens the same renderer in a browser, live.
segments.notes: Contact sheet of ten real Wave stills. Highlight one. Then a live preview window.

segments.title: The chain
sentences: The renderer paints thirty frames a second into a WebM.
The mix ducks the music and lands at minus sixteen LUFS.
The master writes H.264, AAC, chapters and faststart.
The intermediates are not the deliverable. film.mp4 is.
segments.notes: Three stages with real constants. Frame counter, loudness meter, MP4 box.

segments.title: The gates
sentences: Verify is what makes the series trustworthy.
It checks the script hash, and refuses a voice that fell back.
It checks duration, format, chapters, loudness and peak, then the golden frame.
A font fallback or a drifted chapter fails here, not later.
segments.notes: Gate rows check on. Show the two real frames and the SSIM floor. End on a failed gate in coral, then all green.

segments.title: One sentence
sentences: The Wave fixture proves it: same script, same cache, same film.
Change the script, and the timeline moves. The house only moves when you choose.
Every project pins the version that made it.
A sentence goes in. A film comes out. And it can come out again.
segments.notes: Return to the sentence and the frame. The chain folds into a loop. Last line lands in silence.
